title: Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. v. Presbytery of the Ascension
disposition_detail: The Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's judgment sustaining Count 1 by a 10-5 vote and Count 2 unanimously, then remanded for a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examination of the candidate.
first_summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery's approval of an ordination candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate's views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards' teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call's omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate.
summary: Complainants challenged Presbytery's sustaining of ordination trials for a candidate who affirmed continuing revelation through interpreted tongues and its approval of a campus-ministry call lacking required terms. The Assembly sustained both counts, holding that the examination left the candidate's views unclarified and failed adequately to protect the Standards' teaching on the finality and sufficiency of Scripture; Presbytery conceded the call's omission. It remanded the matter to obtain a BCO 21-1-compliant call and re-examine the candidate.

sources.supports: Assembly adoption, undisputed facts, issues, explanatory opinion, count-by-count vote, and both remand directions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The source labels the proceeding Case 5, Complaint of Teaching Elder Carl W. Bogue et al. against Presbytery of the Ascension; lines 77-81 state that the Eighth General Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's minutes as its action and judgment.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 89-107 identify challenges to sustaining Sam Serio's ordination trials despite his views on continuing revelation and to approving a campus-ministry call lacking the written assurance required by BCO 21-1.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 111-139 explain that Presbytery conceded the call defect, that the examination left continuing-revelation views unclarified, and that Count 1 carried 10-5 while Count 2 carried 15-0; the matter was remanded for a proper call and re-examination.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The judgment sustained both counts, although five commissioners voted to sustain only Count 2. The dissent at lines 146-150 disputed the evidentiary support for Count 1 and is not adopted reasoning.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Not applicable; the adopted report does not dispose of the complaint by incorporating another decision.
